name: Rider–Waite–Smith Tarot
art: Pamela Colman Smith, 1909. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

pentacles.name: Pentacles
pentacles.domain: body, money, craft, the material world

single.name: Single card
single.description: One card: a seed to grow an idea from.

positions.name: The card
positions.meaning: The image and theme to work with.

three.name: Past · Present · Future
three.description: The classic three-card line: where it came from, where it is, where it is heading.

positions.name: Present
positions.meaning: The heart of the matter right now.

sao.name: Situation · Action · Outcome
sao.description: A three-card problem solver: what is, what to do, what follows.

story.name: Story Engine
story.description: Five cards for a story, scene or project: who, what they want, what blocks them, the twist, the ending.

positions.name: Resolution
positions.meaning: How it ends, or what is learned.

cross.name: Simple Cross
cross.description: Five cards in a cross: the core, flanked by past and future, with what is above and what lies beneath.

horseshoe.name: Horseshoe
horseshoe.description: Seven cards in an arc, walking from the past through obstacles to the likely outcome.

positions.name: Others
positions.meaning: The people and forces around you.

celtic.name: Celtic Cross
celtic.description: The classic ten-card reading: a cross of the situation and a staff of four cards beside it.

positions.name: Challenge
positions.meaning: What crosses you; the immediate tension.

positions.name: Foundation
positions.meaning: The root beneath; the distant past.

positions.name: Crown
positions.meaning: The best that can be achieved; the conscious goal.

positions.name: Self
positions.meaning: Your attitude and part in this.

positions.name: Hopes and fears
positions.meaning: What you long for and dread, often the same thing.

cards.name: The Fool
cards.imagery: A young traveller in bright clothes steps toward a cliff edge, gazing at the sky, a white rose in hand and a small dog leaping at his heels.

upright.meaning: Step off the edge. Something new starts here, and not knowing is part of the gift.

reversed.meaning: Either you are about to fall without looking, or you are frozen at the edge refusing to jump.

cards.prompt: What would you start if you were sure you could not fail, and did not care how it looked?

cards.name: The Magician
cards.imagery: A figure raises a wand to the heavens and points to the earth; the four suit symbols lie ready on the table before him, an infinity sign above his head.

upright.meaning: Everything you need is already on the table. Channel it into a single act.

reversed.meaning: Talent is misdirected: a con, a performance, or tools left unused.

cards.prompt: Take four things already within reach and make something from only those.

cards.name: The High Priestess
cards.imagery: A veiled woman sits between a black and a white pillar, a scroll half-hidden in her lap, a crescent moon at her feet and pomegranates behind her.

upright.meaning: The answer is not spoken aloud. Be still and listen to what is beneath the surface.

reversed.meaning: A hidden agenda, or an inner voice drowned out by chatter.

cards.prompt: What does the character know but refuse to say?

cards.name: The Empress
cards.imagery: A crowned woman reclines on cushions in a field of ripening wheat, a stream flowing from the forest beside her, a heart-shaped shield with the sign of Venus at her side.

upright.meaning: Growth through care and pleasure. Let things ripen in their own time.

reversed.meaning: Care turned into control, or a garden left untended.

cards.prompt: Describe a place so lush and generous that it changes whoever enters it.

cards.name: The Emperor
cards.imagery: A stern, bearded ruler in armour sits on a stone throne carved with rams' heads, barren mountains behind him, an ankh sceptre in his hand.

upright.meaning: Build the frame. Rules, boundaries and steady leadership make things possible.

reversed.meaning: Order calcified into control, or no structure at all.

cards.prompt: Invent the one law of a kingdom, and the person who would break it.

cards.name: The Hierophant
cards.imagery: A religious figure sits between two pillars, raising a blessing hand over two kneeling acolytes; crossed keys lie at his feet.

upright.meaning: Learn from those who came before. There is wisdom in the form.

reversed.meaning: The old rules no longer fit. Question the institution, or your own blind faith.

cards.prompt: What ritual does a community perform that outsiders would find baffling?

cards.name: The Lovers
cards.imagery: A naked man and woman stand beneath a great winged angel; behind her a tree with a serpent, behind him a tree of flames.

upright.meaning: A meeting of two, and a choice that defines who you are.

reversed.meaning: A rift between heart and principles, or a choice avoided.

cards.prompt: Two people must choose between each other and something they both believe in.

cards.name: The Chariot
cards.imagery: A crowned warrior rides a canopied chariot drawn by two sphinxes, one black and one white, a walled city behind him; he holds no reins.

upright.meaning: Hold opposing forces together by will alone and drive forward.

reversed.meaning: The sphinxes pull in different directions. Force without focus.

cards.prompt: A journey must be completed by an impossible deadline. What drives them on?

cards.name: Strength
cards.imagery: A woman in white, crowned with flowers, gently closes the jaws of a lion; an infinity sign floats above her head.

upright.meaning: Tame the beast with kindness, not force. Quiet strength wins.

reversed.meaning: The lion is loose: fear or fury unmanaged.

cards.prompt: Someone small must calm something enormous and dangerous. How?

cards.name: The Hermit
cards.imagery: A grey-robed old man stands alone on a snowy peak holding up a lantern with a six-pointed star inside, leaning on a staff.

upright.meaning: Withdraw to find the light. The answer is found alone, then shared.

reversed.meaning: Solitude that has become exile, or a refusal to look inward.

cards.prompt: Write the note someone leaves before walking off into the mountains.

cards.name: Wheel of Fortune
cards.imagery: A great wheel inscribed with letters and alchemical symbols turns in the clouds; a sphinx sits atop, a snake descends, a jackal-headed figure rises, and four winged creatures read in the corners.

upright.meaning: The wheel turns. What was down rises; what was up falls. Ride it.

reversed.meaning: Clinging to the wheel, or a downturn you cannot control.

cards.prompt: One coincidence changes everything. What was it?

cards.name: Justice
cards.imagery: A crowned figure in red sits between two pillars, holding upright a double-edged sword and a pair of balanced scales.

upright.meaning: Actions have consequences. Weigh honestly and decide.

reversed.meaning: The scales are rigged, or someone is avoiding the reckoning.

cards.prompt: A verdict is given. Who is it unfair to, and what will they do about it?

cards.name: The Hanged Man
cards.imagery: A man hangs upside down by one foot from a living T-shaped tree, hands behind his back, his face calm and his head surrounded by a halo.

upright.meaning: Stop struggling. Turn things upside down and see them differently.

reversed.meaning: Waiting has become avoidance. Martyrdom without meaning.

cards.prompt: Retell a familiar story from the point of view of its villain or its furniture.

cards.name: Death
cards.imagery: A skeleton in black armour rides a white horse, carrying a banner with a white rose; a king lies fallen, a bishop pleads, and the sun rises between two towers.

upright.meaning: Something ends so that something else can begin. Not literal death: change.

reversed.meaning: Holding on to what is already gone.

cards.prompt: What must be destroyed for the new thing to exist?

cards.name: Temperance
cards.imagery: A winged angel stands with one foot in water and one on land, pouring liquid between two cups; a path winds toward a crown of light on the horizon.

upright.meaning: Mix opposites slowly. The middle way is an art, not a compromise.

reversed.meaning: Too much of one thing. The mixture curdles.

cards.prompt: Combine two things that do not belong together until they make sense.

cards.name: The Devil
cards.imagery: A horned, bat-winged creature squats on a pedestal; a naked man and woman with small horns are chained to it, though the chains hang loosely around their necks.

upright.meaning: The chains are loose. You stay because something in you wants to.

reversed.meaning: Seeing the trap clearly, and stepping out of it.

cards.prompt: What bargain did they make, and what is the fine print?

cards.name: The Tower
cards.imagery: Lightning strikes a tall tower on a crag, knocking off its crown; flames burst from the windows and two figures fall headlong.

upright.meaning: What was built on a lie comes down all at once. It hurts and it frees.

reversed.meaning: The tower cracks but has not fallen yet, or it falls inside you.

cards.prompt: Everything they built collapses in a single night. What survives the rubble?

cards.name: The Star
cards.imagery: A naked woman kneels by a pool beneath a great eight-pointed star and seven smaller ones, pouring water onto the land and into the pool; a bird sits in a tree.

upright.meaning: After the storm, calm. Heal, hope and pour yourself out freely.

reversed.meaning: The star is still there behind the clouds. Look up.

cards.prompt: Write about a small act of hope in a ruined world.

cards.name: The Moon
cards.imagery: A full moon with a face hangs between two towers; a dog and a wolf howl at it, and a crayfish crawls out of a pool onto a winding path.

upright.meaning: Nothing is quite what it seems by moonlight. Trust dreams, but test them.

reversed.meaning: The fog lifts, or a buried fear surfaces.

cards.prompt: Describe a path that is different every time it is walked at night.

cards.name: The Sun
cards.imagery: A naked child rides a white horse beneath a radiant sun, holding a red banner; sunflowers bloom over a garden wall.

upright.meaning: Plain happiness. Everything is visible and warm. Enjoy it.

reversed.meaning: The sun behind a cloud: joy blocked or performed.

cards.prompt: Describe the happiest day of a character's life, and the one detail that makes it real.

cards.name: Judgement
cards.imagery: An angel blows a trumpet from the clouds; below, the naked dead rise from coffins floating on water, arms open to the call.

upright.meaning: A call you cannot ignore. Rise and answer it.

reversed.meaning: The trumpet sounds and you pull the lid back down.

cards.prompt: A long-buried thing is called back to life. What does it want now?

cards.name: The World
cards.imagery: A dancing figure wrapped in a sash floats within a great laurel wreath, holding two wands; the four winged creatures watch from the corners.

upright.meaning: The circle closes. A cycle complete; celebrate before the next begins.

reversed.meaning: The last step remains untaken.

cards.prompt: Write the final scene of something, then the first line of what comes after.

cards.name: Ace of Wands
cards.imagery: A hand emerges from a cloud gripping a sprouting wooden staff; leaves fall from it, and a castle stands on a hill below.

upright.meaning: A spark of pure creative energy is offered. Grab it.

reversed.meaning: The spark sputters. Wait, or find a new fuel.

cards.prompt: Write the first sentence of a project you have never dared start.

cards.name: Two of Wands
cards.imagery: A man on castle battlements holds a globe in one hand and a staff in the other, looking out to sea; another staff is fixed to the wall.

upright.meaning: The world is in your hand. Plan the expedition.

reversed.meaning: Staying behind the walls, globe unused.

cards.prompt: Map a place no one has gone yet.

cards.name: Three of Wands
cards.imagery: A figure seen from behind stands on a cliff among three planted staffs, watching ships sail across a golden sea.

upright.meaning: Your ships are out. Look to the horizon.

reversed.meaning: The ships are late. Plans meet reality.

cards.prompt: Something long awaited finally appears on the horizon. It is not what was expected.

cards.name: Four of Wands
cards.imagery: Four staffs hung with a garland of flowers form a canopy; two figures raise bouquets in celebration before a castle.

upright.meaning: A joyful gathering. Mark the moment.

reversed.meaning: The party feels hollow, or home is unsettled.

cards.prompt: Describe a festival, and the uninvited guest.

cards.name: Five of Wands
cards.imagery: Five young men brandish staffs in a chaotic tussle, none clearly winning or clearly hurt.

upright.meaning: Everyone is talking at once. Messy energy that can sharpen ideas.

reversed.meaning: The scuffle ends, or moves inside.

cards.prompt: Five characters argue about the same thing. Each is partly right.

cards.name: Six of Wands
cards.imagery: A laurel-crowned rider on a white horse parades through a crowd, a wreath tied to his raised staff.

upright.meaning: The win is public. Accept the applause.

reversed.meaning: Pride before the fall, or an unseen victory.

cards.prompt: A hero returns triumphant, but one person in the crowd knows the truth.

cards.name: Seven of Wands
cards.imagery: A man on high ground fights off six staffs thrust up from below, wearing mismatched shoes.

upright.meaning: You hold the high ground. Defend it.

reversed.meaning: Too many attackers. Know when to yield.

cards.prompt: One person defends a position against everyone. Why won't they move?

cards.name: Eight of Wands
cards.imagery: Eight staffs fly through the open sky in parallel over a river and green hills, about to land.

upright.meaning: Things are moving fast. Messages are arriving.

reversed.meaning: Wands stuck in mid-air. Slow down or get unstuck.

cards.prompt: Eight messages arrive at once. Which one changes everything?

cards.name: Nine of Wands
cards.imagery: A bandaged, wary man leans on a staff, guarding a fence of eight more staffs behind him.

upright.meaning: Wounded but standing. One more push.

reversed.meaning: Defending against threats that have passed.

cards.prompt: A veteran guards a gate long after the war ended.

cards.name: Ten of Wands
cards.imagery: A man staggers toward a town bent under a bundle of ten heavy staffs that block his view.

upright.meaning: You are carrying too much. The destination is close; can you put some down?

reversed.meaning: Dropping the load, or being crushed by it.

cards.prompt: What is the heaviest thing a character carries, literally and otherwise?

cards.name: Page of Wands
cards.imagery: A young man in a salamander-patterned tunic studies a sprouting staff in a desert, pyramids in the distance.

upright.meaning: A curious beginner with fire in the belly. Explore.

reversed.meaning: All spark, no follow-through.

cards.prompt: An eager apprentice discovers something their master missed.

cards.name: Knight of Wands
cards.imagery: A knight in salamander-covered tunic rides a rearing horse across the desert, staff held high.

upright.meaning: Charge! Bold, fast and full of fire.

reversed.meaning: Riding off in every direction at once.

cards.prompt: Someone acts first and thinks later. Follow the consequences.

cards.name: Queen of Wands
cards.imagery: A queen on a lion-carved throne holds a staff and a sunflower; a black cat sits at her feet.

upright.meaning: Radiant, independent and magnetic. Own the room.

reversed.meaning: The fire turns inward, or scorches others.

cards.prompt: Write a character who walks into a room and everyone turns.

cards.name: King of Wands
cards.imagery: A king on a throne decorated with lions and salamanders holds a flowering staff, a small salamander at his feet.

upright.meaning: A visionary who turns ideas into movements.

reversed.meaning: Vision without patience; a leader who burns his people.

cards.prompt: A founder's grand vision. What is the cost no one talks about?

cards.name: Ace of Cups
cards.imagery: A hand from a cloud offers a chalice overflowing with five streams; a dove descends with a wafer, and lotus flowers float below.

upright.meaning: The heart overflows. Open to feeling.

reversed.meaning: The cup is tipped or sealed. Feelings held back.

cards.prompt: Describe the moment something first moved you to tears.

cards.name: Two of Cups
cards.imagery: A man and woman exchange cups and pledges; above them hovers a winged lion's head over a caduceus.

upright.meaning: Two meet as equals. A bond is sealed.

reversed.meaning: The toast is off-key. Something is unequal.

cards.prompt: Two strangers discover they share an unlikely secret.

cards.name: Three of Cups
cards.imagery: Three women dance in a circle, raising their cups high amid a harvest of fruits and flowers.

upright.meaning: Friends gather. Raise a glass together.

reversed.meaning: The party goes sour, or someone is left out.

cards.prompt: Three friends toast to something. Each means something different by it.

cards.name: Four of Cups
cards.imagery: A young man sits sulking under a tree, arms crossed, staring at three cups; a hand from a cloud offers a fourth that he ignores.

upright.meaning: Bored with what you have, blind to what is offered.

reversed.meaning: Finally looking up and noticing the gift.

cards.prompt: Someone is offered the thing they always wanted, and says no. Why?

cards.name: Five of Cups
cards.imagery: A cloaked figure mourns over three spilled cups, not seeing the two still standing behind; a bridge leads to a house across the river.

upright.meaning: Mourning what spilled. Two cups remain; turn around eventually.

reversed.meaning: Picking up the remaining cups and crossing the bridge.

cards.prompt: What did they lose, and what did they not notice they still had?

cards.name: Six of Cups
cards.imagery: In an old courtyard, a child offers another a cup filled with white flowers; more flower-filled cups stand around them.

upright.meaning: A gift from the past. Sweet memories, old friends.

reversed.meaning: Nostalgia as a trap. The past was not that golden.

cards.prompt: A childhood object resurfaces decades later. What memory comes with it?

cards.name: Seven of Cups
cards.imagery: A silhouetted figure faces seven cups floating in clouds, each holding a vision: a castle, jewels, a wreath, a dragon, a snake, a veiled figure, a head.

upright.meaning: Too many dazzling options. Most are mirages.

reversed.meaning: The clouds clear; you choose one cup.

cards.prompt: List seven impossible wishes. Pick one and grant it with a catch.

cards.name: Eight of Cups
cards.imagery: Under an eclipsed moon, a cloaked figure walks away from eight stacked cups toward barren mountains.

upright.meaning: Leaving something that is no longer enough, even though it looks fine.

reversed.meaning: Afraid to go, or wandering without a goal.

cards.prompt: Someone leaves a comfortable life in the middle of the night. Where are they going?

cards.name: Nine of Cups
cards.imagery: A well-fed man sits smugly, arms crossed, before a curved table displaying nine cups.

upright.meaning: The wish card. You got what you wanted.

reversed.meaning: Getting your wish, and finding it empty.

cards.prompt: A wish is granted exactly as worded. What goes wrong?

cards.name: Ten of Cups
cards.imagery: A couple embrace with arms raised toward a rainbow of ten cups; two children dance beside them near a cottage.

upright.meaning: Lasting joy, home and belonging.

reversed.meaning: The picture-perfect family has cracks.

cards.prompt: A perfect family photo. What is happening just outside the frame?

cards.name: Page of Cups
cards.imagery: A young man in a flowered tunic stands by the sea, gazing at a fish that pokes its head out of the cup he holds.

upright.meaning: An unexpected, whimsical idea pops up. Play with it.

reversed.meaning: Daydreams that never surface.

cards.prompt: Something absurd appears where it should not be, and it talks.

cards.name: Knight of Cups
cards.imagery: A knight with winged helmet rides a calm white horse slowly forward, holding out a cup like an offering.

upright.meaning: The romantic idealist arrives bearing gifts.

reversed.meaning: All charm, no substance.

cards.prompt: A messenger brings an offer too beautiful to be true.

cards.name: Queen of Cups
cards.imagery: A queen on a throne at the water's edge, carved with sea-nymphs, gazes into an ornate, lidded cup.

upright.meaning: Deep feeling held with grace. Trust the heart's knowledge.

reversed.meaning: Drowning in other people's feelings.

cards.prompt: Write someone who understands everyone except themselves.

cards.name: King of Cups
cards.imagery: A king sits on a stone throne floating on a rough sea, holding a cup and sceptre; a ship sails and a fish leaps behind him.

upright.meaning: Steady amid storms. Mastery of feeling, not suppression.

reversed.meaning: Calm surface, chaos below.

cards.prompt: A leader stays calm while everything floods. What is under their composure?

cards.name: Ace of Swords
cards.imagery: A hand from a cloud holds an upright sword crowned and garlanded; jagged mountains below.

upright.meaning: A clean cut through confusion. The idea is sharp.

reversed.meaning: The sword is dull or wielded carelessly.

cards.prompt: State the single truest sentence you can about your project.

cards.name: Two of Swords
cards.imagery: A blindfolded woman sits by the sea, two swords crossed over her chest; a crescent moon above.

upright.meaning: Blindfolded between two options. Remove the blindfold.

reversed.meaning: The truce collapses; too much to weigh.

cards.prompt: Someone must choose between two equally terrible options.

cards.name: Three of Swords
cards.imagery: A red heart pierced by three swords floats against a grey sky full of rain.

upright.meaning: It hurts. Let it rain; the storm passes.

reversed.meaning: Pulling the swords out, slowly.

cards.prompt: Write the words that broke someone's heart, and what they meant to say instead.

cards.name: Four of Swords
cards.imagery: A knight's effigy lies on a tomb in a church, hands in prayer; three swords hang above and one lies beneath, a stained-glass window behind.

upright.meaning: Lay down your sword. Rest is part of the work.

reversed.meaning: Unable to rest, or resting too long.

cards.prompt: What does a character dream while recovering from a wound?

cards.name: Five of Swords
cards.imagery: A smirking man gathers swords from the ground while two defeated figures walk away toward the sea under a jagged sky.

upright.meaning: You won the fight and lost the friends.

reversed.meaning: Ready to bury the swords.

cards.prompt: The winner of an argument realises they were wrong.

cards.name: Six of Swords
cards.imagery: A ferryman poles a boat carrying a cloaked woman and child toward a distant shore; six swords stand upright in the boat.

upright.meaning: Crossing to calmer waters, carrying your sorrows with you.

reversed.meaning: The boat will not leave the shore.

cards.prompt: Describe a journey taken to escape something. What came along anyway?

cards.name: Seven of Swords
cards.imagery: A man tiptoes away from a military camp carrying five swords, glancing back with a sly grin; two swords remain behind.

upright.meaning: Someone is sneaking. Maybe you. Cunning over force.

reversed.meaning: The thief is found out, or comes clean.

cards.prompt: Plan a heist. What is actually being stolen?

cards.name: Eight of Swords
cards.imagery: A bound and blindfolded woman stands in a ring of eight swords stuck in muddy ground, a castle on a cliff behind her.

upright.meaning: The bonds are loose and the swords do not fully enclose you. Walk out.

reversed.meaning: Taking off the blindfold.

cards.prompt: A prisoner discovers the door was never locked.

cards.name: Nine of Swords
cards.imagery: A figure sits up in bed, face in hands, nine swords mounted on the black wall behind; the quilt is patterned with roses and zodiac signs.

upright.meaning: 3am thoughts. The fear is bigger in the dark than in the day.

reversed.meaning: Dawn after the worst night.

cards.prompt: Write the thought that keeps someone awake at 3am.

cards.name: Ten of Swords
cards.imagery: A man lies face down with ten swords in his back beside dark water; a golden dawn breaks on the horizon.

upright.meaning: It cannot get worse. That is the good news: dawn is coming.

reversed.meaning: Getting up, swords and all.

cards.prompt: Start a story at the very worst moment, then let the sun rise.

cards.name: Page of Swords
cards.imagery: A youth stands on a windswept hill holding a sword upright, glancing over his shoulder; birds fly in the stormy sky.

upright.meaning: Ask questions. Investigate. Stay alert.

reversed.meaning: A sharp tongue without wisdom.

cards.prompt: A young investigator overhears a conversation they were not supposed to.

cards.name: Knight of Swords
cards.imagery: A knight charges at full gallop into the wind, sword raised; trees bend and clouds tear behind him.

upright.meaning: Charging after an idea at full speed.

reversed.meaning: Charging the wrong way.

cards.prompt: Someone rushes in to fix things and makes it worse.

cards.name: Queen of Swords
cards.imagery: A stern queen sits in profile above the clouds, sword upright in one hand, the other hand extended; a single bird flies above.

upright.meaning: Cut through the noise with honest words. No illusions.

reversed.meaning: Honesty turned into a weapon.

cards.prompt: A character says exactly what everyone is thinking.

cards.name: King of Swords
cards.imagery: A king sits facing forward on a throne decorated with butterflies, holding a sword upright and slightly tilted; tall trees and clouds behind.

upright.meaning: Rule by reason. Make the hard, fair call.

reversed.meaning: Intelligence used to dominate.

cards.prompt: A judge must apply a law they know is wrong.

cards.name: Ace of Pentacles
cards.imagery: A hand from a cloud offers a golden pentacle above a lush garden; an archway of roses opens onto mountains.

upright.meaning: A tangible seed: money, a job, a body, a thing you can hold.

reversed.meaning: The coin slips through your fingers.

cards.prompt: Make something real with your hands today, however small.

cards.name: Two of Pentacles
cards.imagery: A young man dances while juggling two pentacles linked by an infinity loop; ships ride high waves behind him.

upright.meaning: Keep everything in the air with a light step.

reversed.meaning: Too many balls.

cards.prompt: A character must keep two lives going at once.

cards.name: Three of Pentacles
cards.imagery: A stonemason works on a cathedral arch while a monk and an architect holding plans consult with him.

upright.meaning: Build it together. Each skill matters.

reversed.meaning: The team is out of sync.

cards.prompt: Three experts with different skills must build one thing together.

cards.name: Four of Pentacles
cards.imagery: A crowned man clutches a pentacle to his chest, one balanced on his head and two under his feet; a city behind him.

upright.meaning: Holding on tight. Safety, or a cage?

reversed.meaning: Opening the hand, or losing the grip.

cards.prompt: What would a miser never part with, and what makes them finally let go?

cards.name: Five of Pentacles
cards.imagery: Two ragged figures, one on crutches, trudge through snow past a lit stained-glass window showing five pentacles.

upright.meaning: Out in the cold. Help is near, if you look up at the window.

reversed.meaning: Coming in from the cold.

cards.prompt: Two outcasts pass a warm, lit door. Why don't they knock?

cards.name: Six of Pentacles
cards.imagery: A merchant holding balanced scales gives coins to one of two kneeling beggars.

upright.meaning: Give and receive in fair measure.

reversed.meaning: Help that comes with power games.

cards.prompt: A gift comes with hidden conditions.

cards.name: Seven of Pentacles
cards.imagery: A farmer leans on his hoe, looking at seven pentacles growing on a leafy bush.

upright.meaning: Pause and look at what you have grown. Is it worth continuing?

reversed.meaning: Doubting the harvest.

cards.prompt: Years of work. Was it worth it? Write the honest answer.

cards.name: Eight of Pentacles
cards.imagery: An apprentice sits at a bench carving pentacles, six displayed on a post beside him, one more at his feet.

upright.meaning: Practice. One more, a little better than the last.

reversed.meaning: Grinding without growth.

cards.prompt: Do the same small exercise eight times. Notice what changes.

cards.name: Nine of Pentacles
cards.imagery: An elegant woman in a flowered robe stands in a vineyard heavy with grapes and pentacles, a hooded falcon on her gloved hand.

upright.meaning: You earned this garden. Enjoy your own company.

reversed.meaning: A gilded cage.

cards.prompt: A character at the peak of success, alone in their garden. What do they think about?

cards.name: Ten of Pentacles
cards.imagery: An old man in a patterned robe sits with two dogs under an archway; a couple and a child stand nearby, ten pentacles arranged in the Tree of Life.

upright.meaning: What lasts beyond you: home, lineage, tradition.

reversed.meaning: The inheritance divides the family.

cards.prompt: A will is read. One item causes a feud.

cards.name: Page of Pentacles
cards.imagery: A young man stands in a green, ploughed field gazing intently at a pentacle held up in both hands.

upright.meaning: A diligent student with a practical dream.

reversed.meaning: Staring at the coin and never spending it.

cards.prompt: What would you learn if you had a full year with nothing else to do?

cards.name: Knight of Pentacles
cards.imagery: A knight sits motionless on a heavy black horse in a ploughed field, holding a pentacle and looking at it.

upright.meaning: Slow and steady. Show up every day.

reversed.meaning: The horse has stopped moving.

cards.prompt: Write the most boring hero imaginable, and make them win.

cards.name: Queen of Pentacles
cards.imagery: A queen sits in a flowering garden on a throne carved with goats and fruit, cradling a pentacle in her lap; a rabbit runs at her feet.

upright.meaning: Warm, practical care. A home where people thrive.

reversed.meaning: Caring for everything but yourself.

cards.prompt: Describe a kitchen and the person who runs it.

cards.name: King of Pentacles
